basis.reason: The approved plan explores the design direction, so the concept is open and three territories are drawn (Design §48.2).

territories.thesis: The familiar lender page done properly: the loan range, a cost check you can use before giving any details, three plain steps and the facts that earn trust, all on one calm, well-set page.
territories.meaningInterpretation: The trust requirement 'show the cost before the form' is answered by putting the cost check in the first screen beside the promise, and 'show who decides and how fast' by stating the one-working-day decision as a fact, not a badge.
territories.audienceExperience: A wary shop owner sees in five seconds what Tillwell lends, that the cost is shown before applying, and how long it takes; nothing asks for their details until they choose to start.
territories.composition: One column of 1200 centred. A two-part hero: the promise and range on the left, the cost check card on the right. Then a three-step strip, a facts band, what you need to apply, and a closing call to start.
territories.typography: IBM Plex Sans throughout, chosen for plain, legible figures; a 52px display, 32px section heads, 18px body. Numbers are set at the display or figure size so they read before the words around them.
territories.artDirection: No photography; the shop is present through words. Shape is solid and slightly rounded, like a counter top, with thin rules rather than shadows.
territories.colourAndMaterial: White page, deep green ink for calm, a pale green panel for the cost card, and one warm rust for every action. Never red near money.

signature.noneBecause: The cost check card is the page's one strong element; a signature device would compete with it.

territories.addressesBrief: Shows the full cost before the form, the range, the one-day decision and no early-repayment fee in the first screen, then makes starting an application obvious.
territories.deliberatelyNot: No trust badges or review scores (the owner gave none), no stock handshakes, no gradients, no small print.
strengths: Every owner fact is visible above the fold
weaknesses: Looks like the category, only better made
risks: Without a rate from Tillwell the cost card shows a placeholder until the rate is supplied
implementationImplications: The cost check needs Tillwell's pricing table to compute a real total

territories.thesis: The home page is an indicative quote: three answers about your shop and the total cost appears, in pounds, on a printed-looking sheet, before Tillwell asks who you are.
territories.meaningInterpretation: The desired memory, 'they showed me the cost before asking for anything', becomes the structure: the quote is the page, and everything else explains it.
territories.audienceExperience: The owner moves an amount and a term and watches a plain sheet fill in: what you borrow, what you repay, the fee for paying early (none), and when you hear back. Applying is the next line on the sheet.
territories.composition: Dark navy page; a two-column first screen of 1240 centred, the inputs on the left and the white quote sheet on the right, larger, like paper on a counter. Below, one row that says who decides and how fast, and what you need.
territories.typography: Manrope for words and Source Serif 4 for the figures on the sheet, so amounts read as a written quote rather than a dashboard.
territories.artDirection: No imagery. The sheet is the image: white paper, ruled lines, figures aligned right.
territories.colourAndMaterial: Deep navy for the page so the white sheet stands out; a warm orange for the one action; muted blue-grey for labels.

signature.device: The quote sheet: ruled lines with each cost on its own line and the total underlined twice.

territories.addressesBrief: Cost transparency before any personal data is the first thing the page does, and the decision time and early-repayment rule are lines on the quote.
territories.deliberatelyNot: No hero headline over a picture, no three-step strip, no sign-up wall before the quote.
weaknesses: Relies on the quote being computed; until Tillwell supplies rates it shows placeholders
risks: A dark page can feel heavy; kept calm with generous space
tradeoffs: Less room for explanation in the first screen
implementationImplications: Needs Tillwell's pricing to compute; the sheet must stay readable at 200% zoom

leaders.takes: A calculator that shows repayments before sign-up
leaders.transformed: Shown as a written quote sheet with the total in pounds, not a slider widget beside a rate

leaders.takes: An offer presented as already worked out
leaders.transformed: Worked out from three answers about the shop, with no personal data
Each cost on its own ruled line so nothing is folded into an APR

territories.thesis: Speak to shop owners as shop owners: the page opens on what the money is for (stock before a busy season, a refit, a new fridge) and prices each in pounds before it shows a single loan term.
territories.meaningInterpretation: Answers the gap rows: the total cost in pounds is the headline, and the words are about shops, not 'SMEs'. Plain language is the design.
territories.audienceExperience: An owner recognises their own reason to borrow on the first screen, picks it, and sees the amount and what it would cost to repay, then the facts that make it safe to apply.
territories.composition: Full-width first screen on a pale sage page: a very large headline in a grotesk, then a row of four reason tags, each opening its own cost line below. The rest of the page is short: the decision time, no early fee, what you need.
territories.typography: Archivo at a large display size for the voice of a shop sign, and Archivo at body sizes; figures in the same face, heavier.
territories.artDirection: Shop-tag shapes for the reasons; no photographs.
territories.colourAndMaterial: Sage page, deep green ink, and a price-tag yellow for the one action and the selected reason.

signature.device: Price tags: each reason to borrow is a tag that turns over to show what it costs.

territories.addressesBrief: Leads with the shop's reason and the cost in pounds, then the facts that build trust, then the application.
territories.deliberatelyNot: Breaks the floor's 'hero with a loan range and an apply button' (f1): the range and the button come after the owner has seen a cost for their own reason.
strengths: Fills both gaps in the field
weaknesses: Reasons are draft words the owner must confirm
risks: An owner whose reason is not listed must still find their way: an 'something else' tag is always there
tradeoffs: Less like a bank, which some owners may read as less serious
implementationImplications: Each reason needs an amount Tillwell is comfortable showing as an example

ruleBroken.why: Owners burned by hidden fees distrust a range and a button; seeing a cost for their own reason first is what earns the click.
ruleBroken.safeguard: The range and the start button appear directly under the reasons, and 'Start an application' is in the header from the first screen.
